name: application-skip-links
title: Skip Links
description: Hidden keyboard shortcuts that appear on focus to let users bypass repeated navigation and jump directly to main content.
useWhen: Every page or view has a navigation region that keyboard users would otherwise have to tab through repeatedly.
Adding baseline keyboard accessibility to any application shell with a persistent header or sidebar.
avoidWhen: There is no repeated navigation to bypass — a single-page form does not need a skip link.
The page has only one interactive region — skip links are most valuable on pages with multiple landmarks.
responsiveBehavior: Skip links are visually hidden at all viewport sizes and become visible only when they receive keyboard focus. Ensure the visible state renders above all other page content.
accessibility: Skip links must be the first focusable elements in the document so they appear at the top of the tab order.
The href target must match the id of the destination landmark (e.g., <main id='main-content'>).
Skip links must be visible — not just programmatically focused — when they receive keyboard focus.

variants.title: Basic skip link
variants.description: A single 'Skip to main content' link that is visually hidden until focused, the standard minimal implementation.
accessibility: Must be the first focusable element in the document; visible on focus; href targets <main> by id.

variants.title: Multiple skip links with dark background
variants.description: A set of skip links on a dark background offering multiple bypass targets such as navigation, search, and main content.
accessibility: Multiple skip links let keyboard users jump to specific landmarks; each target id must exist in the page.

variants.title: Skip links with title and light background
variants.description: Skip links with an accessible section title on a light background, visually styled as a visible banner when focused.
accessibility: Section title is visible on focus along with the links; background color must contrast with the link text.
